jrandolf opened PR #14868 from jrandolf:implements-docs-tests to bytecodealliance:main:

This fixes docs around implements and named imports that had drifted from the implementation, and adds tests for paths that had no coverage.

Docs:

  • ComponentExternData::implements said it's used to match imports by interface name, but imports are only resolved by their own name.
  • The bindgen! named_imports docs said the id is passed by reference and that interfaces with resources aren't supported. Neither is true anymore. They now also explain how labelled imports are bound with and without named_imports.
  • The WASI named views (WasiNamedView, WasiHttpNamedView and the per-interface ones) said their ResourceTable doesn't need to be shared. It has to be the default context's table, because resources flow between named and plain interfaces; for example, a stream from a named wasi:cli/stdout is used through wasi:io/streams.
  • The config and CLI flag docs now mention external-id next to implements, and a few typos are fixed.

Tests:

  • The bindgen! implements test now actually puts (implements ...) on its imports. Before, they were plain imports.
  • An interface exported twice under different labels, called through bindgen!.
  • The Linker resolves a labelled import only by its label, never by the interface it implements (and vice versa), and two labels get separate definitions.
  • Semver edge cases for ComponentExtern::is_implements.
  • Loading a precompiled component that uses implements into an engine with the feature disabled fails, and external-id is rejected when the feature is disabled.

None of the new tests found a bug. I checked that each one fails against a deliberately broken implementation.

Closes #14857

:speech_balloon: alexcrichton created PR review comment:

Is there any particular reason to test the deserialize behavior vs assuming it works?

:speech_balloon: alexcrichton created PR review comment:

If this is true, this might be a bug -- separate imports are supposed to get separate traits. Lacking this option means that the host can only load the WIT of the shape that was passed in to bindgen!, and the presence of this option means that the host can load components with a variety of shapes of WIT (e.g. arbitrary named keys). -- I think this is the important distinction to make here, if at all.

:speech_balloon: alexcrichton created PR review comment:

Are you sure this isn't already tested? IIRC this was added when I first added implements support (or at some point)

:speech_balloon: alexcrichton created PR review comment:

:speech_balloon: alexcrichton created PR review comment:

Why is "(including resource destructors)" necessary here?

:memo: alexcrichton submitted PR review:

I'd ask you to please be judicious when adding tests for tests sake. There's an infinite amount of things we could test but we have limited CI resources. It's not worth it to test everything possible, so tests need to carry their weight beyond "seems good".

:speech_balloon: alexcrichton created PR review comment:

I think the wording here (and replicated elsewhere) is a bit too strong. While I think it's worthwhile to say that it's recommended that there's only one table it's not strictly required. For example wasi:clocks can work with separate tables I believe due to the resource types being part of the interfaces.

Could this (and other blocks) be re-worded to say that a single table is strongly recommended, but not required in all situations?

  • The config and CLI flag docs now mention external-id next to implements, and a few typos are fixed.

It also fixes the bindgen! implements tests, whose component didn't actually annotate its imports with (implements ...), and checks that external-id is rejected when the feature is disabled.

:speech_balloon: jrandolf created PR review comment:

I checked: it is the case today, and it's by design from #13497. I think it also matches the spec's intent for hosts: the guest gets distinct per-label names, while the host can serve every label with one implementation parameterized by the label, which is what named_imports provides. Different backends per label are still possible with add_to_linker_instance. So I've left it as is, and the docs now describe the distinction you mentioned.
